premises.statement: Law properly regards order to common good.
Ordering the multitude to common good belongs to it or its public caretaker.
Ordering to an end belongs to the one whose proper end it is.
A person can be a law to himself participatively by sharing in a regulator’s order.
The legislator aims to lead people toward virtue.
A private person can advise, but rejected advice lacks coercive force.
The multitude or public caretaker has coercive power to impose penalties.
A household is part of the city, the complete community.
A household governor can set precepts, but they do not thereby have proper law character.
The objection moves from natural performance of law’s works and self-as-law to private lawmaking.
The objection moves from anyone encouraging virtue to anyone being a legislator.
The objection analogizes the household governor to the city ruler.
The sed contra defines law as a people’s constitution enacted with the people.
